With XBLOCK=128, each warp issues 4 scalar 32-bit loads, leaving 128-bit vector load bandwidth on the table. NCU reports only 26.4/32 bytes utilized per L2 sector (uncoalesced/non-vectorized), and 78.4% of warp stall cycles are L1TEX scoreboard waits. Increasing XBLOCK to 1024 and adding tl.max_contiguous + tl.multiple_of hints tells the Triton compiler that the xindex range is contiguous and aligned, enabling it to emit 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads/stores. This reduces the number of memory transactions by 4x, cuts L1TEX stall cycles, and reduces grid launch overhead from 6.78M to 848K blocks.
